chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We only spread cushions with images on them in our homes and spread them out.' He said, 'There is no harm in what is spread, laid out, and trodden upon from them; but what is disliked from them is that which is set up on the wall or on the bed.'

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: Images or statues, specifically figurative representations

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between images that are permissible and those that are disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a functional distinction in the prohibition of images (tathmil), ruling that they are permissible when used as floor coverings or cushions because they are trodden upon, thereby diminishing their status. This contrasts with images mounted on walls or beds, which are disliked due to their prominent display and honor. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the context of usage and the degree of reverence accorded to the image rather than a blanket prohibition.
